fields.features_heading: What the Sheet Collects at the Door
fields.features_subheading: Paper grids get retyped the week school starts. Emergent builds a sign-in that fills the class contact list as families arrive.
fields.feature_1:
One question per screen at the door

Shows each family one question at a time on the tablet by your door or on their own phone. A parent holding a toddler answers the student's name, then their own, then a phone number.
fields.feature_2:
A live list of who has not come yet

Checks every sign-in against the class roster you give it and keeps a running list of families still missing. By the time the room empties, that list is your follow-up list.
fields.feature_3:
The welcome packet for families who miss it

Emails your welcome packet link to each family still on the missing list at the time you choose, such as 8:00 AM the next morning. Nobody has to chase the packet by hand.
fields.feature_4:
How each child gets home on day one

Asks whether the child rides in a car, takes a bus, goes to after-care or walks, and asks bus riders for the bus number. The dismissal list sorts the class by that answer.
fields.feature_5:
Volunteer roles that close when full

Gives each volunteer role a set number of spots, such as 2 room parents. When a role fills, the next family sees only the roles that still have open spots and picks from those.
fields.feature_6:
A class list you own, and its code

Saves every sign-in to a database you own, so the list carries into conferences and field trip forms. On paid plans, export the full code of the sheet to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Classrooms on Meet the Teacher Night
fields.tab_content_1:
Each family that missed the night gets the packet by 8:00 AM

Ardith Pilkvist has 22 children on her kindergarten roster at Quarrybend Elementary. Families sign in on the tablet by her door, and 18 come to meet the teacher night. The 4 who stay home are still on the missing list when the room empties, and each gets her welcome packet by email at 8:00 AM.
fields.tab_content_2:
On day one, the dismissal list sorts 24 children

Second graders at Ellsmoor Elementary go home four different ways. As each of Thorvald Bergqvist's 24 families signs in, it picks how the child leaves on day one, and bus riders add a bus number. His list sorts the class into 10 car riders, 8 bus riders, 4 for after-care, and 2 walkers.
fields.tab_content_3:
A third room parent request turns into a chaperone spot

Eustacia Ludgate needs 2 room parents and 4 field trip chaperones for her fourth grade class at Brambling Elementary. Leopoldine Fothergill and Rhodri Nethercott sign in first and take room parent, which now shows 2 of 2 taken. Mirabel Underhill signs in next and takes a chaperone spot, leaving 3 of 4 open.
fields.tab_content_4:
One contact list, grouped by home language

Fintan Ainsworth has 26 families sign in for his sixth grade homeroom at Inchcape Middle School. The sheet asks which language each family wants school notes in: 19 pick English, 5 Spanish, and 2 Korean. His contact list groups families by that answer, so the family liaison sees which 7 notes need a translated copy.

faq_heading: Meet the Teacher Sign-In Sheet FAQ

plan.angle: The top 10 for meet the teacher sign in sheet is decorative printables from TPT, Etsy, Pinterest and Scribd: a grid with student name and parent name that the teacher types up by hand after the night. This page treats the sheet as the first entry in the class contact list: a kindergarten teacher whose 4 absent families get the welcome packet by email the next morning, a second grade dismissal list sorted by how each child gets home, volunteer roles that close when full, and the language each family wants home notes in. The FAQ covers what to ask, sign in on a phone or tablet, families who miss the night, privacy of contact details and keeping the list for the year.
tab_stories: At Quarrybend Elementary, 18 of kindergarten teacher Ardith Pilkvist's 22 families sign in on the tablet by her door, and the 4 who did not come get her welcome packet by email at 8:00 AM the next morning.

At Ellsmoor Elementary, each of second grade teacher Thorvald Bergqvist's 24 families picks how their child gets home on the first day, and his dismissal list sorts 10 car riders, 8 bus riders with bus numbers, 4 after-care and 2 walkers.

At Brambling Elementary, fourth grade families pick a volunteer role as they sign in for Eustacia Ludgate's class, and once both room parent spots are taken the next family is offered a field trip chaperone spot.
At Inchcape Middle School, 26 families sign in for Fintan Ainsworth's sixth grade homeroom and pick a home language for school notes, and his contact list groups the 5 Spanish and 2 Vietnamese picks.
